records.rate_definition: Chinese yuan per 1 US dollar; Federal Reserve H.10 New York noon buying rate. Percentage change is calculated as (ending rate / starting rate - 1) * 100, rounded to two decimal places.

source.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise numerical observations and source links only.

limitations: The starting observation is from https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h10/20250106/ published 2025-01-06; the source field links to the ending observation.
The percentage is calculated from two observations, not reported by the Federal Reserve; it is a change in yuan per US dollar, not the inverse currency return.
The endpoints do not describe the intervening rate path or volatility; archived releases may not reflect subsequent data revisions.
Reference rates do not establish any selected supplier's invoicing currency, conversion rate, hedging, or actual cost impact.

records.rate_definition: Philippine pesos per 1 US dollar; Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas published rates. Percentage change is calculated as (ending rate / starting rate - 1) * 100, rounded to two decimal places.

source.licence_notes: Redistribution terms not independently verified; concise numerical observations and source links only.

limitations: BSP's monthly end-of-period table gives both rates; the starting rate is also in the 31 January bulletin at https://www.bsp.gov.ph/Lists/RERB/Attachments/1959/31Jan2025.pdf and the ending daily value appears at https://www.bsp.gov.ph/statistics/external/day99_data.aspx.
The peso comparison begins on 31 January 2025, not 2 January 2025 as for the Federal Reserve pairs; the two date intervals are not identical.
The percentage is calculated from two observations, not reported by BSP; it is a change in pesos per US dollar, not the inverse currency return.
The endpoints do not describe the intervening rate path or volatility; the BSP web tables can be updated.
BSP rates use a different source and convention from the Federal Reserve rates; reference rates do not establish supplier invoicing, hedging, or actual cost impact.
